guidance_issued_by: Oklahoma Legislature (SB 1734, Responsible Technology in Schools Act) with implementation guidance from the Oklahoma State Department of Education
unique_context: The Oklahoma Responsible Technology in Schools Act (SB 1734, signed May 12, 2026, effective July 1, 2026) is one of the few enacted K-12 AI statutes: AI may be used for instruction only under educator direction, may not be the primary basis for grading, discipline or promotion, parents may opt students out of student-facing AI tools without penalty, and districts must disclose AI vendors and data collected annually. Every district and charter must adopt a board-approved written AI policy before the 2027-28 school year; OSDE is to issue implementation guidance. Non-compliance risks eligibility for state-funded programs.
notes: Before the statute, OSDE had published advisory 'Guidance and Considerations for Artificial Intelligence in Oklahoma Schools' (2024) with an AI acceptable-use rating scale. Most other 2026 Oklahoma AI bills (deepfakes, chatbot protections for minors, agency oversight) stalled, partly under a federal executive order discouraging state AI regulation.
